records.name: Carmen Loyola
records.bio: Loyola is one of the authors or compilers of the 2014 UNAM institutional history used in the Mexico module. The book documents the historical didactic collection of the Museo Nacional de Historia Natural and identifies Blaschka glass models including Radiolaria and Aurelia aurita.
records.open: The exact page text should still be checked against an official or physical copy of the 2014 book.

records.name: Hilda Flores Olvera
records.bio: Flores Olvera is one of the authors or compilers of the 2014 UNAM institutional history used to trace the Mexico City collection. The publication supplies institutional and didactic context for surviving Blaschka models in the later UNAM collections.
records.open: The exact page text should still be checked against an official or physical copy of the 2014 book.

records.name: Antonio Lot
records.bio: Lot is one of the authors or compilers of the 2014 UNAM institutional history used in the Mexico module. The publication helps connect the former Museo Nacional de Historia Natural didactic collections to Blaschka models surviving in later university custody.
records.open: The exact page text should still be checked against an official or physical copy of the 2014 book.

records.name: Chris Rowley
records.bio: Museums Victoria object records name Rowley as the person who identified two stored glass models as Blaschka works on 17 January 2019: Serpula vermicularis and Eledone moschata. Those identifications provide direct modern object-level anchors for the Melbourne collection.
records.open: Candidate historical Blaschka catalogue numbers remain taxon-level matches pending local label verification.

records.name: Edward Ayer
records.bio: A secondary study with an exact Henry Augustus Ward Papers citation names Ayer as a signatory to the 18 November 1893 contract between Ward’s Natural Science Establishment and the Columbian Museum of the City of Chicago. The contract belongs to the broader transfer context from which the Field Museum’s Blaschka material emerged.
records.open: The primary contract scan has not yet been captured in the backend, and the signatory evidence is therefore retained through the cited secondary source rather than promoted to an item-specific Blaschka purchase claim.

records.name: M. Nowak-Kemp
records.bio: A peer-reviewed study credits Nowak-Kemp, courtesy of the Oxford University Museum of Natural History, for the photograph of an Oxford Anthea cereus Blaschka model acquired in 1867. The image is a direct visual anchor for one of the earliest documented British sea-anemone models.
records.open: The backend preserves only the initial M.; fuller authority reconciliation remains to be done.

records.name: Stuart Humphreys
records.bio: Humphreys is credited by the Australian Museum for photographs attached to several Blaschka sea-anemone records and reference images. Those official visual records are used in the backend as object and instance-group documentation rather than as additional physical-object counts.

records.name: V. Marquardt
records.roles: photographic credit · Museum der Universität Tübingen
records.bio: The Tübingen eMuseum credits Marquardt on its numbered Blaschka object record for Aulosphaera elegantissima, IEÖ-Zo-21. The project retains that credit as part of the model’s official digital-media record and rights history.
records.open: The backend preserves only the initial V.; fuller authority reconciliation remains to be done.

records.name: Jean Spielmann
records.bio: The Geneva module records Spielmann or the initials ‘js’ in the issue context for a detailed local history of the Geneva Blaschka collection. The article preserves useful figures for the 1888 acquisition, shipment, price and later display history, but its article-level authorship still requires checking.
records.open: Article-level authorship is not yet fully verified against the issue masthead and should remain qualified.
